documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology and oncology practice. Return visit 01/09/2025.

30-year-old with celiac disease and iron deficiency anemia, treated with IV iron a year ago, referred back. About six months of fatigue, looking pale per her family, and breathlessness with exertion. She describes her periods as regular with a moderate flow. She eats little red meat by choice.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. NKDA.
Family: father type 1 diabetes, mother autoimmune thyroiditis, maternal aunt celiac.

Exam: pale, with pale conjunctivae. No lymph node enlargement. Liver and spleen not palpable.

Labs: Hgb 9.2 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, RDW 18%. Peripheral smear: microcytic, hypochromic red cells. Iron 30 mcg/dL, TIBC 600 mcg/dL, ferritin 8 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 5%.

Assessment: recurrent iron deficiency anemia; malabsorption from celiac disease with recent gluten exposure, limited dietary iron, menstrual losses.
Plan: repeat ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV x2, one week apart. Continue oral iron. CBC and ferritin in 2 months via PCP. Continue strict gluten-free diet.

documents.title: Infusion Center Record
documents.author: hematology
documents.body: Infusion summary. 01/16/2025 ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, tolerated. 01/23/2025 ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, tolerated; course complete. No hypersensitivity reactions. Post-infusion labs at PCP in about 8 weeks.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 31F.

IV iron again in January, energy back within a few weeks. Strict about gluten now: has her own toaster, packs lunch every day, gloves for playdough. Bowels normal, no bloating. Weight up to 58 kg, best she has felt in years. Cramps and bone aches gone on vitamin D. Periods still heavy for 2-3 days, ibuprofen helps. She and her partner are talking about trying for a baby in the next year or so; she knows to talk with endo first about tighter sugars.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro per scale, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, cholecalciferol 2000 u daily, calcium carbonate 500 bid, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.
PHQ-9 1.

Exam: well, good color. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. Feet: sensation and pulses normal.

A/P
1. Recurrent IDA - CBC/ferritin today after second IV course. Continue oral iron.
2. Celiac - tTG today to check adherence.
3. T1DM - endo. TSH, microalbumin, lipids.
4. Vitamin D deficiency - on maintenance via endo.
5. Preconception: advised to loop in endo and to see us when ready.
6. HM: Pap due 2026. Flu/COVID in fall.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 12.0, ferritin 74, nice response. tTG 9, now normal: diet is working. TSH, urine microalbumin and lipids normal. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, visit 05/13/2025.
Type 1 diabetes. She and her partner are planning a pregnancy in the coming year. A1c 6.8%. Preconception targets reviewed: A1c under 6.5% if achievable without lows, folic acid once trying or at the first positive test per her PCP and obstetrician, early obstetric referral. Continues cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro, ferrous sulfate, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate, ibuprofen as needed. NKDA.
Plan: tighten pre-meal targets gradually; call with a positive test. Return 4 months.

conditions.label: Acute dacryocystitis of right lacrimal passage

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days
medications.reason: Acute dacryocystitis, right; prescribed in the emergency department

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 06/26/2025 19:40. Discharged 22:05.

Chief complaint: right eye swelling.

HPI: 31-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, celiac disease and iron deficiency anemia, followed in GI and hematology clinics. Three days of pain, redness and swelling at the inner corner of the right eye with watery discharge, and her vision on that side is a little blurry. No fever, no injury, no recent illness. Diabetes well controlled on insulin per patient.

Meds: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, preschool teacher.

Vitals: afebrile, hemodynamically normal.
Exam: Right medial canthus: erythema and tenderness over the lacrimal sac; pressure over the sac expresses pus from the punctum. Visual acuity slightly reduced on the right compared with the left. No foreign body seen. Conjunctiva otherwise quiet, cornea clear, pupils equal and reactive, extraocular movements full and painless, no proptosis. Left eye normal.

MDM: presentation consistent with acute dacryocystitis of the right lacrimal sac, no signs of orbital involvement.

Disposition: discharged home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg by mouth twice daily for 10 days. Warm compresses with gentle massage four times a day. Ophthalmology follow-up within a few days; return for fever, worsening swelling, eye pain with movement or further vision loss. Glucose checks as usual. Copy to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit. Seen in the ED Thursday night for a red, swollen right inner eye corner, told it was an infected tear sac. On amoxicillin-clavulanate since Thursday, day 4 of 10. Much less swollen, discharge almost gone, vision clearer. No fever. Sugars a little higher over the weekend, now settling.

Exam: afebrile. Right medial canthus with mild residual redness, minimal tenderness, no fluctuance, no discharge expressed today. Eye movements full and painless. Conjunctiva quiet. Vision grossly equal.

A/P: Acute dacryocystitis, right, improving on oral antibiotic. Finish the 10 days, warm compresses. ED asked for ophthalmology follow-up: referral placed, office reached and seeing her Thursday. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology. Seen 07/03/2025.
Referred after ED diagnosis of right acute dacryocystitis, now on day 7 of amoxicillin-clavulanate.
Swelling and discharge nearly resolved. Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS with correction, back to her baseline. Minimal residual erythema at the right medial canthus, no tenderness, no reflux from the punctum on pressure. Anterior segment quiet. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy.
Assessment: right acute dacryocystitis, resolving.
Plan: complete antibiotic course. No further intervention now. Return promptly if swelling or discharge recur.

documents.title: Staff health form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Our center needs the staff health form again before September. Uploading it now. Eye is totally fine by the way.

documents.title: RE: Staff health form
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Got it, Lauren. Signed by the doctor from your March physical and sent back through the portal. Glad the eye cleared up.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning, I just got a positive home pregnancy test! First day of my last period was September 1. We were trying. I already emailed endo. What do I do first? Should I keep taking the ibuprofen and all my pills?

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Please stop the ibuprofen for now; acetaminophen is the safer choice for cramps or aches. Keep your insulin, iron, vitamin D and calcium. I have you Thursday at 3:30 so we can confirm, start folic acid and get you to obstetrics quickly, which matters with type 1.

orders.reason: intrauterine pregnancy about 5 weeks, pre-existing type 1 diabetes

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31F G1, LMP 9/1/25, so about 5w4d. Positive home test Monday, planned. No bleeding, no pain. Stopped ibuprofen. Endo already moved up her visit and is tightening targets.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro per scale, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, cholecalciferol 2000 u daily, calcium carbonate 500 bid. NKDA. No alcohol since trying.

Exam: well. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P
1. Early pregnancy with pre-existing T1DM - high-risk; referral to obstetrics placed today, they will arrange MFM input and dating ultrasound. Folic acid 1 mg daily started. A1c, TSH, CBC today. Endo co-managing insulin.
2. Recurrent IDA - continue iron; CBC today.
3. Celiac - stable on diet.
4. Right dacryocystitis in June - resolved, off the active list.
5. Flu and COVID vaccines given today, both recommended in pregnancy.
Acetaminophen as needed instead of ibuprofen.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.5, TSH normal, Hgb 11.9. Copied to OB and endo. Message to pt.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound. Single intrauterine pregnancy. Crown-rump length corresponds to 8 weeks 3 days, consistent with dates by LMP. Fetal cardiac activity present. Adnexa unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Single live intrauterine pregnancy, 8w3d, concordant with LMP. EDD 06/08/2026.

documents.title: Obstetrics New Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology group, high-risk prenatal clinic. New OB visit 10/30/2025.

G1P0 at 8w3d by LMP 09/01/2025, confirmed by ultrasound today. EDD 06/08/2026.
History: type 1 diabetes since childhood (endocrinology co-managing), celiac disease on a gluten-free diet, iron deficiency anemia treated with IV iron, vitamin D deficiency on maintenance, heavy menses.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate, ibuprofen as needed (listed). NKDA.

Prenatal labs: Hgb 11.6; HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen and syphilis screen negative; urine culture no growth. All within normal limits.

Plan: low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily beginning at 12 weeks given pre-existing diabetes. Detailed anatomy ultrasound at 18 to 20 weeks. Shared glucose logs with endocrinology every 1-2 weeks. Return 4 weeks.

documents.title: Endocrinology Pregnancy Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, visit 11/25/2025, 12 weeks pregnant.
Type 1 diabetes in pregnancy. A1c 6.2%. Some first-trimester lows mid-morning; lispro ratios at breakfast adjusted down, correction scale tightened for pregnancy targets. Glargine continues.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro, ferrous sulfate, folic acid, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate, aspirin 81 mg starting this week per OB. NKDA.
Plan: logs to us every 2 weeks; we will adjust as insulin needs rise in the second and third trimester.
